mission.objective:
Fix this Python stats utility. Create exactly four tasks: Designer, then Coder,
then independent Reviewer and Security tasks. The runtime handles integration
after their gates; do not schedule an extra integration-confirmation task.
Designer: read README.md and stats.py, then provide an implementation contract.
Coder: run check 0 BEFORE edits and observe the failure, fix mean, add median
(odd/even/empty), replace eval with safe JSON parsing as specified in README,
and add regression tests for each requirement including malicious input rejection.
Reviewer and Security: independently inspect the changed code and run check 0;
provide actual evidence and a verdict. Parsing is high risk. Only modify stats.py
and tests/**. Finish the reviewed, tested, integrated mission.

tasks.description: Read README.md and stats.py, inspect existing tests, and identify the configured check 0 from maestro.toml. Provide an implementation contract covering correct mean behavior, median for odd, even, and empty inputs, README-specified JSON parsing and error handling, and malicious input rejection. acceptance: The contract references the relevant README requirements and identifies defects in stats.py.
Expected behavior and regression cases cover mean, odd/even/empty median, safe JSON parsing, and malicious input rejection.

tasks.summary: Implementation contract: modify only stats.py and tests/**; use Python standard library only. Coder must run configured check 0 BEFORE any edits and record its actual failure, then implement and rerun it. Exact command: /usr/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v (configured argv: ["/usr/bin/python", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests", "-v"]). mean(values) must divide sum(values) by len(values), preserving ValueError for empty input. Add median(values): sort a copy, return the middle value for odd length, the average of the two middle values for even length, and raise ValueError for empty input; avoid mutating caller input. Replace eval with json.loads; require the decoded root to be a list and each element to be an int or float but never bool, reject all other element types, and reject non-finite floats. Reject JSON NaN/Infinity/-Infinity constants (for example using a rejecting parse_constant callback) and also check decoded floats for overflow such as 1e400. Treat ints as finite without converting arbitrary-size ints to float. Invalid JSON and prohibited content must raise ValueError; no code evaluation or execution paths. Return the decoded list preserving numeric values. Regression tests: mean([2,4,6]) == 4, mean([7]) == 7, mixed signed/fractional mean and empty mean; unsorted odd median [9,1,5] == 5, even [8,2,6,4] == 5, singleton and empty median, and input unchanged. Parsing positives include [1,2.5,-3], [], whitespace, and exponent notation. ValueError cases include malformed JSON, Python-only syntax, non-list roots (object, number, string, null, boolean), booleans within lists, nested lists, strings, objects and null elements, NaN/Infinity/-Infinity, and overflow exponents of both signs. Add malicious-input rejection with an expression such as __import__('builtins').print('executed') and assert both ValueError and no execution side effect using a mock of print; also reject expression-bearing array input such as [__import__('builtins').print('executed')]. Independent Reviewer and Security must inspect changed code and tests and each run check 0, reporting actual results and verdicts; Security should specifically inspect parser type checks, bool rejection, constants, overflow, and malicious-input non-execution. No extra integration-confirmation task is needed; runtime integrates after gates.
